Union City Council District 3
# Together, let's build a Union City that works for all of us!
Endorsed by neighbors, educators, community leaders and electeds.
Get Involved
## Why I'm Running
Union City deserves competent, empathetic leaders who represent the shared values of our community — values rooted in listening, compassion, accountability, and honesty. I am a community-driven leader who understands our neighborhoods, residents, and businesses. I will work collaboratively to create a safe, equitable, and vibrant city for the next generation.
We need leaders who are proactive, who take courageous stances on the issues that matter, and who aren't satisfied with the status quo when it isn't serving our residents.
I built my priorities by listening across every corner of our community from town halls, to district dialogue meetings and in conversations with our District 3 neighbors. My platform is rooted in your experience, because you deserve nothing less.
I'm running because I believe Union City's best days are ahead of us — and because this community deserves a leader who will fight for every family, every neighborhood, and every voice that has gone unheard. I'm that leader, and I'm ready to go to work for you.
### My Priorities
- A Safer, Cleaner Union City — Strengthening public safety, eliminating blight, and keeping our neighborhoods well-maintained
- Smart Growth & Fiscal Accountability — Responsible development, transparent budgeting, and securing the infrastructure funding our city was promised
- Thriving Families & Strong Schools — Championing quality public education, youth programs, and support for working families
- Community Voice & Civic Power — Elevating neighborhood voices, expanding civic engagement, and ensuring every resident has a seat at the table
## Rooted in Union City
I'm the daughter of union parents — UFCW and IBEW — and I learned early that when working people show up, communities get stronger. Our family is rooted in District 3, in the Old Alvarado neighborhood, where we're raising our two daughters in my husband's childhood home. After 17 years in Union City, this isn't just where we live — it's who we are.
I have a Master's in Business Administration and have more than 20 years of experience in construction and finance. I served on Union City's Park & Recreation Commission for five years and was the commission's Chair from 2023-2024. That combination, real-world budget discipline and hands-on governance experience, is exactly what City Council decisions demand. I've managed complex projects, navigated regulatory environments, and learned how city policy shapes the daily lives of our residents.
But my deepest qualification is the work I do as a neighbor. As an educational foundation board member, PTO president, Girl Scout troop leader, lead advocate for Bond Measure N, and champion for local small businesses and green space — I've spent years building connections and lifting the voices that make Union City extraordinary.
Read My Full Story
## A Vision for Union City
Rooted in Community, Ready for Our Future
A leader who combines 17 years of neighborhood roots in District 3 with the professional expertise to secure Union City's long-term resources, infrastructure, and fiscal health.
A Safer, Cleaner, More Connected Union City
A commitment to strengthening public safety, investing in a cleaner city, and delivering the transportation and infrastructure improvements our residents were promised.
Real Solutions for Our Neighborhoods
Addressing the tangible, everyday issues that affect District 3 families — from business development and permitting, to pedestrian safety and clean streets, to parks and public services — through proactive outreach, data-driven problem-solving, and direct advocacy.
## Where I Stand
Our community faces real challenges — and you deserve a councilmember who will tackle them head-on. Here's how I'll fight for District 3.
### Transportation, Infrastructure & Safety
Safe streets don't happen by accident. I'll deliver on Measure B's promises, improve railroad crossings, and keep the momentum on school traffic safety.
Learn More →
### Housing & supportive services
Our city needs a strategic, regional approach to eliminate homelessness and expand support for our most vulnerable residents.
Learn More →
### Public Safety
Union City's declining crime rate reflects our police department's hard work — and I intend to build on that progress with the right resources and smarter prevention.
Learn More →
### Clean & Green City
The way our city looks reflects the pride we take in our community — and right now, we can do better. I'll fight for the funding and systems to keep Union City clean and beautiful.
Learn More →
### Union City as a Destination
Union City has world-class diversity, rich history, and a vibrant small business community — but you'd never know it from how we market ourselves. That changes now.
Learn More →
### Community Voice & Civic Power
Union City's greatest untapped resource isn't in the budget — it's in our neighborhoods. I'll make sure every resident has a seat at the table.
Learn More →
## Get Involved Today
If my story resonates, join our grassroots campaign! Let's work together for Union City.

## In the Community
Safe streets don't happen by accident — they take advocacy, follow-through, and leaders willing to bring the right people to the table. I've done it before, and I'll keep doing it as your councilmember.
Fix the basics: Potholes, lighting, pedestrian crossings, and parking. I'll push for concentrated, responsive attention to District 3's most pressing everyday road and safety needs.
Deliver on transportation's promise: Union City has fought hard for regional funding and a vision for the future. I'll make sure we capture every dollar we're owed — to keep our city safe, accessible, modernized, and moving forward. I will continue to advocate for additional funding to be used where our neighborhoods need it most.
Improve railroad crossings: Our railroad crossings are in need of modernization. I'll advocate for the safety upgrades that reduce congestion and bring Union City up to the standard our residents deserve.
Keep the momentum on school traffic safety: After a year of advocacy — bringing the school district and city traffic engineers to the same table — we redesigned drop-off zones, a parking lot, and pedestrian safety features in one of the city's most congested corridors. In months, not years. I'll keep that momentum going at every school site in District 3.
Union City's two full-time outreach employees are a strong start — but our city needs a strategic, regional approach to eliminate homelessness and expand support for our most vulnerable residents.
Build regional partnerships: No single city can solve homelessness alone. I'll work to establish partnerships with neighboring cities and Alameda County to create a sub-regional housing and support network that shares resources, data, and best practices.
Establish local safety nets: I'll identify locations and funding for temporary and transitional housing within or near Union City — providing immediate relief and a clear path toward permanent housing, including rapid re-housing models proven in comparable communities.
Expand outreach & close service gaps: Our outreach employees need a growth plan behind them. I'll assess and close gaps in local mental health services, addiction treatment, and crisis intervention — so no resident in crisis falls through the cracks.
Union City's declining crime rate reflects our police department's hard work — and I intend to build on that progress with the right resources, the right partnerships, and smarter prevention.
Listen to our public safety leaders: My first action on public safety will be sitting down with the Police Chief and frontline officers to understand their resource needs — staffing, technology, training, and budget alignment. Good policy starts with listening.
Integrate public safety & human services: Police shouldn't be the only responders to mental health or homelessness crises. I'll work to establish local partnerships that put trained crisis intervention professionals alongside law enforcement.
Invest in proactive prevention: I'll champion our current community district policing model, visible neighborhood patrols, support community neighborhood watch programs coupled with education and outreach, and push for data-driven strategies that target crime before it happens. Yet safety means more than patrol cars — it means thriving neighborhoods. I will advocate and champion prevention that tackles the root causes of crime, making sure our communities are resourced and heard.
The way our city looks reflects the pride we take in our community — and right now, we can do better. I'll fight for the funding and systems to keep Union City clean, green and beautiful.
Dedicate real funding to cleanliness: I support allocating up to $1 million annually to combat trash accumulation, illegal dumping, and median beautification. This is a budget priority I'll fight for with a clear line item in every cycle.
Launch a clean city rapid response team: When residents report a problem, the response should be measured in days, not weeks. I'll push to establish a dedicated team focused solely on timely removal of bulky trash and illegal dumping.
Expand green infrastructure: I'll advocate for expanded green space, sustainable landscaping, and partnerships that keep our city clean and environmentally responsible for the next generation.
Champion recycling in our schools: A green city starts with our kids. I'll work with New Haven Unified School District to strengthen and expand recycling programs across our school district — building environmental habits early and modeling the values we want to see citywide.
Union City has world-class diversity, rich history, and a vibrant small business community — but you'd never know it from how we market ourselves. That changes now.
Champion small business: Local businesses are the backbone of our neighborhoods. I'll work to reduce barriers, streamline permitting, and create visibility for the shops, restaurants, and entrepreneurs that make Union City unique.
Celebrate our culture and history: I'll push for programming, public art, and events that celebrate Union City's multicultural heritage and position us as a cultural destination in the East Bay.
Enhance the City's digital presence to attract visitors: Union City's website and online presence should showcase our local art, cultural destinations, and small businesses — a dynamic platform that drives visitors and investment to our community.
Union City's greatest untapped resource isn't in the budget — it's in our neighborhoods. I've spent years registering voters, volunteering, organizing neighbors, and building coalitions around common causes. As your councilmember, I'll bring that same energy to City Hall — civic engagement isn't a talking point for me. It's how I've lived my life in District 3.
Elevate underrepresented voices: The residents most affected by city decisions are often least represented in the room. I'll build intentional outreach to renters, immigrants, seniors, and working families — ensuring their priorities shape city policy. I aim to create real, structured pathways for residents to shape the decisions that affect their daily lives.
Bring City Hall to the neighborhood: Government should come to you — not the other way around. I'll hold regular District 3 town halls and mobile office hours across our neighborhoods, where residents actually are. When people feel heard, they show up.
Build a culture of civic participation: I'll champion voter registration drives, multilingual civic education, and partnerships with schools, faith communities, and local organizations — so every resident sees city government as something they drive, not something that happens to them.
Transparent, accountable governance: You deserve to know how decisions are made and how money is spent. I'll push for clear public reporting on council votes, budget decisions, and city contracts — and hold myself to that same standard.

### Cheris Crocker-Root — Full Bio
×
## A Proven Advocate for Families, Equity, and Community Voice
Cheris Crocker-Root is a proud Union City resident, community advocate, and mother of two young daughters attending public school in New Haven Unified School District. She lives in the same District 3 home where her husband was raised, a testament to her family's deep roots and long-term commitment to Union City.
Raised by union parents — members of UFCW and IBEW — Cheris grew up understanding the value of hard work, equity, and public service. Her childhood was spent in a politically active household where she learned to phone bank, canvass, and organize for local issues and national campaigns. She carried those values with her across a career in both private and public sectors, and throughout decades of volunteer service across the Bay Area.
### Rooted in the Bay Area, Committed to Union City
Although raised in Seattle and Bremerton, Cheris spent every summer since 1985 with her family in San Francisco and the East Bay. She moved to Daly City in 2000, to Oakland in 2003, and finally made Union City her home in 2009. Her lived experience across diverse Bay Area communities informs her commitment to responsive and inclusive leadership for Union City.
### Community Involvement
She is the current President of the Alvarado Elementary School Parent-Teacher Club, a School Site Council voting member, and an active participant in:
- New Haven Schools Foundation (Board of Directors)
- City of Union City Green Team
- Parent advisory groups and educational initiatives
### Professional Experience That Delivers Results
Cheris brings over two decades of cross-sector leadership experience in construction & finance in areas of project management, asset management, property management, and employee experience and DEI development programs:
- Asset Manager & Investor Relations (4 yrs) — Currently managing over 630 multifamily housing units and $20 million in equity as lead for a private multifamily real estate firm founded in the Bay Area, operating across four states.
- Project Coordinator (9 yrs) — Led strategic initiatives, diversity programs, and employee development programs within the Corporate Properties Group of a major bank with an international portfolio of 70 million square feet and 1,200 employees.
- Finance, Marketing & Project Management (12 yrs) — At a Bay Area construction firm specializing in commercial tenant improvements, hospital retrofits, and data centers. Cheris worked her way up from accounting and HR to project management, operations, and business development while earning her MBA from the University of Phoenix, Oakland Campus.
- Consulting for Property Management (17 yrs) — For a private owner, managing leasing from move-in to move-out with 100% positive tenant and building owner relations, continuing to manage the building and its construction for 11 more years — resulting in zero broken leases and zero evictions through the building's sale in 2024.
### Public Service & Leadership Roles
Cheris has worked to serve and build community across Union City:
- Appointed Park & Recreation Commissioner (2019–2024)
- Interview Panelist for Alvarado Elementary School Principal (2024)
- Interview Panelist for Director of Community & Recreation Services, Union City (2025)
- Interview Panelist for Assistant Superintendent, Business (2025)
- Principal for Bond Measure N (2024) — to support local school funding
- Campaign volunteer and organizer for Union City council races and regional elections
### Political & Civic Engagement
Cheris believes that representation matters — and that local government should reflect the voices of everyday residents and live in the district they represent. She proudly serves as:
- Alternate to Scott Sakakihara on the Alameda County Democratic Central Committee
- Member, Tri-Cities Democratic Forum
- Member, Ohlone Area United Democratic Club
- Member, Alameda County Progressives
- Member, Strategies for Change Subcommittee, ADCC
- CADEM, Children's Caucus
- CADEM, Progressive Caucus
- CADEM, Women's Caucus
- CADEM, Labor Caucus
- Volunteer, Youth Voter Movement
